messages.subject: Nested random effects
parts:
Hi Group members,
I would like a model with 2 random nested effects, considering this example below:
library(INLA)
dat <- expand.grid(A=1:4,B=1:8)
dat$Y <- c(rnorm(4,0,4) %*% t(model.matrix(~as.factor(A)-1,dat)) + rnorm(8,0,2) %*% t(model.matrix(~as.factor(B)-1,dat)))
dat
dat$AB <- paste0(dat$A,dat$B)
m0f <- Y ~ 1 + f(A,model='iid',constr = T) +f(AB,model='iid',constr = T)
m0 <- inla(m0f,data=dat)
summary(m0)

m0$summary.random$A
m0$summary.random$AB

in this case, we have restriction for sum of effects = 0 for each variance component independently .
It is possible in component AB, restrict for sum of effect u_i = 0 for each level of A?

Thanks 
Éder

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Nested random effects
parts:
sure. since A is in the set 1,2,3, you can just use 'replicate', which
will replicate the model over A, which is iid with sum to zero.

attached is a test
H

*********

AA=4
BB=8
dat <- expand.grid(A=1:AA,B=1:BB)
dat$Y <- c(rnorm(AA,0,4) %*% t(model.matrix(~as.factor(A)-1,dat)) +
rnorm(BB,0,2) %*% t(model.matrix(~as.factor(B)-1,dat)))

f(A, model="iid", diagonal=0, constr=T) +
f(B, model='iid',replicate=A, diagonal=0, constr = T)

m0 <- inla(m0f, data=dat)

print(sum(m0$summary.random$A[, "mean"]))
for(a in unique(dat$A)) {
print(a)
print(sum(m0$summary.random$B[1:BB + (a-1)*AA, "mean"]))

}

I added the argument 'diagonal=0' to ensure that no diagonal element is
added because of the constr=T. usually, the constr is used for
intrinsic models which a small extra value for the diagonal is
required. howeveer, the value is added by default is small, so it does
not do any harm...
